axes.model_access:
**Supports cloud and local LLMs — can connect to almost any model, with an explicit local-model option.**

**Official wording (translated)**: "the models the README currently recommends are Claude 3.7 Sonnet, DeepSeek R1 & Chat V3, OpenAI o1 / o3-mini / GPT-4o"

**Note: this recommendation list is stuck on the previous generation of models.**

That is consistent with the project not having shipped a release for 13 months.

Verify currently available models yourself when referring to this list.
axes.runtime:
**A local Python process running in the terminal; its lifetime is bound to the terminal session.**

Quit the terminal and it ends.

It is the PyPI package `aider-chat`.

Official badges show 6.8 million installs.

There is also a long-running watch mode (see the [IDE-form entry](../../coding/products/aider.md)).
axes.local_files:
**Repo Map is this tool's core mechanism.**

It is a concise map of your entire git repository.

**Official wording**: "Aider makes a map of your entire codebase, which helps it work well in larger projects."

The map contains **the most important classes and functions with their types and call signatures**.

**Every time the user requests a change, the repo map is sent to the model along with the request.**

The map contains the repository file list plus the key symbols of each file.

The docs explicitly list **two purposes**:

- helping it understand the code being edited and how it relates to the rest of the codebase
- helping it **reuse existing libraries, modules and abstractions** when writing new code

Supports 100+ programming languages.

**File access scope**: what it can edit are the files you `/add` to the chat.

The repo map scans the entire git repository.

Scanning is constrained by `.gitignore` / `.aiderignore`: `--aiderignore` points at the ignore file (default: `.aiderignore` at the git root); `--subtree-only` considers only the current subtree.

The repository must be a git repository.

**Official wording (translated)**: "without git it first asks whether to create one."

**The map's token budget is controlled by `--map-tokens`; refresh frequency by `--map-refresh` (auto/always/files/manual).**

**For large repos, actual time and token cost: the official gives no numbers, and this site has not measured them.**
axes.background:
**No background long-running tasks in the terminal form.**

There is a watch mode (see the [IDE-form entry](../../coding/products/aider.md)): a long-running process watching file changes and responding to AI comments in the editor.

**But that is a local process staying resident, not a cloud background.**
axes.tools:
**File editing + Git operations.**

**The README stresses that Git integration is itself a core feature.**

It automatically commits with sensible commit messages.

You can also use familiar git tools to diff, manage and undo AI changes.

The official docs also have `docs/languages.md` (language support) and `docs/git.md`.

**Configurable lint / test commands run automatically**:

- `--lint-cmd` / `--auto-lint` (runs lint on edited files by default)
- `--test-cmd` / `--auto-test`
- `/run` runs a shell command and optionally adds the output to the chat
- `/web` fetches a web page and converts it to markdown
- `/paste` pastes an image

The docs source is `docs/usage/lint-test.html`.

**No built-in MCP support**: neither the official options table nor the docs-site navigation has any MCP entry (checked `config/options.html` and the docs directory).

So it cannot connect to MCP servers.
axes.context:
**Repo Map provides a whole-repo structural view, attached to every request** (see local_files).

**When context overflows it uses "summarization" rather than simple truncation.**

**Official wording**: "Soft limit on tokens for chat history, after which summarization begins"

That line is the official description of the `--max-chat-history-tokens` option.

That is: past the soft limit summarization begins; summaries are generated by `--weak-model`.

Each model's context window and cost are supplied by `--model-metadata-file`.

In-session: `/tokens` shows usage; `/drop`, `/clear`, `/reset` free space.

**No cross-launch restore by default** (`--restore-chat-history` defaults to False).

Chat history is written to `.aider.chat.history.md` by default.
axes.permissions:
**Auto-commits by default** (`--auto-commits` defaults to True).

This is its integrated design, not an add-on feature.

`--dirty-commits` (default True) first commits existing uncommitted changes as well.

The undo path is **git itself**, not a rollback feature provided by the tool.

**Official wording**: "Use familiar git tools to easily diff, manage and undo AI changes."

In-session use `/undo`.

**A confirmation layer exists**: the official provides `--yes-always` (alias `--yes`).

**Official wording**: "Always say yes to every confirmation"

That is: by default it asks about certain operations; only with this switch does it go fully automatic.

`--dry-run` previews without changing files.

**No sandbox mechanism**: the official options table has no sandbox entry.

Apart from the lint / test commands you configure (`--auto-lint` / `--auto-test`), it does not autonomously run arbitrary shell commands (`--suggest-shell-commands` only suggests).
axes.fit:
**Fits three scenarios.**

**Changes kept in git**: you want AI changes to always stay under git version control.

Such changes are diffable and undoable.

**Multi-model access**: users who need local models or multiple cloud providers.

**Reusing existing abstractions**: people who want "reuse existing abstractions when writing new code".

That is also Repo Map's second purpose.

**Not a fit if you need active maintenance or new-model support** (see the maintenance status below).

sections.⚠ 维护状态（本条目最重要的信息）:
**Conclusion: this project has entered maintenance status and should not be treated as an active project.**

The basis follows.

| Metric | Value | From collection date |
|---|---|---|
| Latest release | `v0.86.0` | **2025-08-09 (13 months ago)** |
| Previous release | `v0.85.0` | 2025-06-27 |
| Last commit | expanding the ANTHROPIC_MODELS list | 2026-05-22 |
| Stars | 49,702 (rolling re-check 2026-10-23) | — |
| PyPI installs | 6.8 million | — |

**Judgement: lifecycle = `maintenance`**

Reasons:

- no release for 13 months
- the last few commits are **maintenance changes** (expanding model lists), not feature development
- the README's model recommendations are still on the previous generation (the Claude 3.7 Sonnet era)

**This does not mean "broken", but it means**:

- new-model support may lag
- new language / framework adaptation may lag
- bugs may not get fixed upstream

**When citing this entry for a selection decision you must weigh this.**

| Capability | Official wording highlights |

| **Cloud and local LLMs** | can connect to almost any LLM, including local models |
| **Repo Map** | generates a structural map of the entire codebase, helping it work well in larger projects |

sections.Repo Map 是它的差异化能力:
**Official wording**: "Aider makes a map of your entire codebase, which helps it work well in larger projects."

This differs from other tools' "fetch files on demand" approach: **build a whole-repo structural map first, then work from it**.

**Note**: A6.2 has verified — **the token budget is controlled by `--map-tokens`** (set to 0 to disable); refresh frequency by `--map-refresh` (auto/always/files/manual).

**How files are selected and ranked into the map** is explained in the official `docs/repomap.md`.

This site has not verified it line by line, and the official gives no numbers for actual cost on large repos either.
sections.Git 集成是设计的一部分，不是副作用:
**Official wording**: "Aider automatically commits changes with sensible commit messages." "Use familiar git tools to easily diff, manage and undo AI changes."

**This deserves emphasis on its own**: many tools leave git management to the user.

Aider treats "auto-commit + undo via git" as the core workflow.

**This brings a prerequisite you must know**: AI changes go **straight into the commit history**.

If you are not comfortable with git's undo flow (`git reset` / `git revert`), try it on a small repository first.
sections.官方自我评价的一个有趣指标:
**Official wording**: "Percentage of the new code in Aider's last release written by Aider itself"

**Official badge wording**: "🔄 Singularity — 88%"

That is: "88% of the new code in the last release was written by **Aider** itself".

This is the officially self-reported bootstrapping degree — a reference point, not to be over-read.
